title: Management Information Systems, B.S. (Business)
notes: This major was named 'Management Information Systems, B.S.' through the 2024-25 catalog and was not renamed to 'Business Analytics and Information Systems, B.S.' until the 2025-26 catalog -- the live/2026 bulletin URL 404s for every archive year before 2025-26 under the current slug, exactly as expected. Before assuming 'the major didn't exist,' confirmed this is a rename rather than a different program: this page's own <meta name="keywords"> tag reads 'MIS_BS, MIS' -- the identical plan code (MIS_BS) the live 2025-26/2026-27 Business Analytics and Information Systems bulletin page also carries -- and it is filed under the same department (Supply Chain and Information Systems) offering the same core MIS-prefixed course sequence (MIS 250/301/431/432/441/446/479W). So this is real continuous history of the same program under its old name, not a fabricated backfill. University Park track only (this archived page's own Suggested Academic Plan is titled 'at University Park Campus'; a separate 'at Commonwealth Campuses' plan on the same page is the 2+2-feeder version for students starting elsewhere, not modeled here -- same convention as the current BAIS-2026.json only modeling the University Park plan). Fetched via raw curl + regex table parse (not WebFetch's summarizer) and cross-checked against the page's own printed per-term subtotals (15/14/17/15/15/15/14/15 = 120 total) before transcribing -- all match exactly. Curriculum differences from the current (2025-26+) BAIS plan, confirmed by this fetch: (1) no MIS 437 course existed yet (it was introduced in the 2025-26 revision) -- Third Year Spring's course-alternative pairing is 'MIS 441 or 446' / 'MIS 446 or 441', placed one per term in Fourth Year (not Third Year) exactly as BAIS-2026.json already documents doing for its own 'MIS 437/446' and 'BA 411/MIS 441' pairs; (2) the 'Business Breadth Course' terminology did not exist yet -- this page literally prints 'Two-Piece Sequence (see Department list)' with no footnote and no linked list anywhere on this archived page (unlike the current bulletin's footnote 5, which points to a real Smeal Business Breadth list) -- modeled as an honest generic 3cr placeholder slot (same convention BIOL-2026.json uses for its own unenumerated 'Supporting Courses' range) rather than reusing BAIS-2026.json's Business-Breadth 'match' regex, since that specific enumerated list is a 2025-26+ Smeal artifact this archived page gives no evidence existed in 2022-23; (3) BA 411 (a real, singly-listed 'Prescribed Course' in this page's own Program Requirements table, not a repeated one) is printed with a '(or Two-Piece Sequence (see Department List))' annotation in BOTH Fourth Year terms on the flowchart -- reconciled by placing BA 411 once (Fourth Year Fall) and a second generic breadth/Two-Piece slot in Fourth Year Spring, so the plan's total generic-breadth-labeled credits (this one + Third Year Spring's) sum to exactly 6, matching this page's own Program Requirements table line 'Select 6 credits of supporting coursework. See Department List.' -- rather than double-booking BA 411; (4) Fourth Year Fall's Gen Ed slot is tagged '(Z)' on this page (this catalog's now-retired 'Linked' inter-domain designator; footnote 4 here reads '6 credits of Inter-Domain (N) and/or Linked (Z) coursework', so Z and N are the same underlying Inter-Domain requirement bucket) -- mapped to this app's existing 'INTER-D' gen_ed key, same as every '(N)' slot elsewhere in this plan and in BAIS-2026.json. Same real prereq-chain gap as BAIS-2025.json/BAIS-2026.json applies here too (it is a property of MATH/SCM/STAT/ACCTG's actual prerequisites, not of any one catalog year): SCM 200/STAT 200/ACCTG 211's real prereq is MATH 21, absent from this plan otherwise, and MATH 21 itself real-chains through MATH 4 and MATH 3 -- added MATH 3 (Semester 1) and MATH 4/MATH 21 (Semester 2) explicitly, same placement BAIS-2025.json/BAIS-2026.json already use. Bumped max_credits_per_semester from 17 to 18, same reasoning and same value as BAIS-2025.json/BAIS-2026.json, to keep 4-year graduation achievable with the added 9 credits. 'etm' marks this page's own Entrance-to-Major footnote-2 courses.
